lead: # The dedup GUARD, not an optimization: identical name and size is a hint, a hash is the proof. The
# first real run of the JavaScript this ports found 1902 files with identical name AND size and
# different bytes.
# A hard link shares metadata, so the shared inode has to adopt the group's NEWEST mtime or every
# non-canonical tree reads its artifact as stale and rebuilds it. std cannot set an mtime.
# `bsc-disk` — the build tree's garbage collector, and the parked-worktree pool's cap.
# A LEAN, standalone crate (like `bsc-self` and `bsc-project`): the shared CLI scaffold, a hash, and
# a way to set mtimes. It touches no Tauri and no database, so it stays out of the DuckDB build path
# and a scoped `cargo check -p bsc-disk` is seconds rather than minutes.
sections.name: [dependencies]

lead: # build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# THE SHARED CRATE ROOT — this crate owns no source file at all. See
# crates/graph-materialize/crate_root.rs; the crate's own docs come from its record.
# THE TEST SOURCE IS IN THE GRAPH, not in this directory
# (`the-integration-test-targets-become-edges`). `tests/real_trees_parity.rs` does not exist: the
# whole file is the `bsc-disk-pool-prune-unit-dedupe--realTreesParity` EDGE in graph/algorithms.json,
# which also records the four member records it spans. The shared build script materializes it into
# `$OUT_DIR/tests/real_trees_parity.rs` and the shared root below `include!`s it, so `cargo nextest`
# compiles and runs it as an ordinary integration test — from OUTSIDE the crate, against the public
# API, which is what a `tests/` target is for.
# `tests/real-trees.parity.json` DOES stay on disk: it is the corpus, not a target, and the record
# reaches it with `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/tests/…")` — a bare relative `include_str!`
# would resolve against `$OUT_DIR/tests/` once materialized and find nothing.
sections.name: [[test]]
